issue.title: Mockito.after() method accepts negative timeperiods and subsequent verifications always pass
issue.body:
e.g.

```
Runnable runnable = Mockito.mock(Runnable.class);
Mockito.verify(runnable, Mockito.never()).run(); // passes as expected
Mockito.verify(runnable, Mockito.after(1000).never()).run(); // passes as expected
Mockito.verify(runnable, Mockito.after(-1000).atLeastOnce()).run(); // passes incorrectly
```

input.args: Issue 197: Mockito.after() with negative millis (after(-1000).atLeastOnce()) makes verification pass incorrectly. Source: mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java after(long) calls new After(...); After.java passes it to VerificationOverTimeImpl; internal/util/Timer.java validateInput throws cannotCreateTimerWithNegativeDurationTime (Reporter.java) when durationMillis < 0.

findings.summary: Timer rejects negative durations, so after(-1000) should throw instead of letting verification pass.
findings.failure_scenario: after(-1000).atLeastOnce() calls new Timer(-1000) via After and VerificationOverTimeImpl, which throws cannotCreateTimerWithNegativeDurationTime rather than passing silently. The reported silent pass does not match this commit.
